sm: Bioethics lawyer Wesley J. Smith warns about a new organ procurement method called donation after cardiac death. Under the long-standing dead donor rule, organs can be taken only from the deceased and no one may be killed for that purpose. In the new process, once the heart stops after life support is removed, the arteries to the brain are clamped and the heart is then restarted to preserve the organs. Smith says this violates the rule both ways, since a restarted heart means the patient was not dead, and clamping the arteries causes brain death. The American College of Physicians said the burden of proof for the practice has not been met. Because some patients showed signs of life, regulators allowed puncturing donors' arteries as a second safeguard, and Smith fears weakening the rule will lead to fewer donors.

This part presents remarks from Robert F. Kennedy Jr. He says he has read horror stories of people certified as dead who woke up during organ transplants. He describes his nephew, who had cerebral palsy, choked and was declared brain dead, and whose organs saved five people. Kennedy says losing public trust in transplant organizations is a crime because people then stop donating. He says another organization is in line for decertification, and that the national agency called OPTN became corrupt, with a contractor sharing an overlapping board. All fifty-four organizations must now have a patient safety officer and a whistleblower hotline. He says people skipped the waiting line, and that doctors and procurement companies profit, so corruption must be guarded against. A note adds that new rules starting December sixth require clamping and severing blood vessels to a donor's brain, after doctors reported signs of life.
